column_semantics: For floating-rate debt, the schedule separates Reference Rate, Spread, and Interest Rate. PIK is printed as a component inside the Spread column, while the Interest Rate column prints the total all-in rate including reference rate, cash spread, and PIK. For fixed/all-in-rate positions, the schedule uses an All-In Rate column and parenthetically identifies 100% PIK when applicable.

rationale: The filing does not use the stated Interest Rate column as the cash leg only. On floating-rate rows, PIK is appended in the Spread column, and the separate Interest Rate column prints a larger all-in total. For example, Deerfield shows SOFR with Spread 3.00 %, 2.75 % PIK and Interest Rate 9.45 %; Ellkay shows SOFR with Spread 3.25 %, 3.50 % PIK and Interest Rate 10.60 %. The dedicated All-In Rate header and Integrity's 10.50 % (100 % PIK) row confirm that position-level stated rates are all-in totals when printed as rate columns.
